correctness.rationale: Pointwise conjugation with phases (1,i) gives explicit complementary nonzero idempotents P1=(T-iI)/(1-i), P2=(I-T)/(1-i), with P1+iP2=T an isometry although 1+i is nonzero; the phase pair (1,-1) fails isometry on the constant i, whose image has norm sqrt(5). The general proof correctly distinguishes complex-linear blocks, where the quadratic spectral relation is required, from conjugate-linear blocks, where complementary idempotency is equivalent to T^2=I. Under the standard C^1 coordinate isometry, this yields the stated exact Form IV criterion and the mixed Form II/III criteria.

originality.rationale: The inspected arXiv:2609.18967v1 states the antipodal-or-BCI dichotomy and semilinear BCI conclusions, but the explicit conjugation example contradicts them. Exact and synonymous searches did not locate a public correction of the v1 or the stated semilinear block repair. Botelho--Miura 2019 is acknowledged as strong prior art for an earlier incomplete GBCI classification, and older real-linear/nonlinear idempotent literature remains the principal residual risk for the elementary interpolation lemma.

value.rationale: The result corrects the main abstract-level dichotomy of a current functional-analysis preprint and replaces an isolated contradiction with a reusable semilinear mechanism. It gives an exact corrected criterion for the fully conjugate Form IV and identifies the blockwise repair for the mixed forms without disturbing the complex-linear Form I case.
